subject: Mathematics

sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: We the Travellers — I When was the last time you went on a long trip?
sections.source_evidence: We the Travellers — I When was the last time you went on a long trip?

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: Ask the elders who went with you to help you answer these questions.
sections.source_evidence: Ask the elders who went with you to help you answer these questions.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: Human beings have always been interested in travelling.
sections.source_evidence: Human beings have always been interested in travelling.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: About a hundred years ago, there were far fewer vehicles than today.
sections.source_evidence: About a hundred years ago, there were far fewer vehicles than today.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: There were animal-drawn carts, cars, and trains.
sections.source_evidence: There were animal-drawn carts, cars, and trains.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: Long before this, thousands of years ago, people travelled long distances on foot or used animals to travel from one place to another.
sections.source_evidence: Long before this, thousands of years ago, people travelled long distances on foot or used animals to travel from one place to another.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: They also built boats and ships to travel across lakes, rivers, and seas.
sections.source_evidence: They also built boats and ships to travel across lakes, rivers, and seas.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Boats were probably the first form of transport invented by humans, much before bullock carts!
sections.source_evidence: Boats were probably the first form of transport invented by humans, much before bullock carts!

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: Do you know how many vehicles are currently there in your state?
sections.source_evidence: Do you know how many vehicles are currently there in your state?

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Reading and writing large numbers How do you write numbers to show several thousand objects?

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: What numbers do we get when we keep adding a thousand?

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: We use the same ten digits 0–9 in different places to write larger numbers.

sections.content: Let us see how we write numbers beyond 10,000 and how we name them.
